body: Guatemalan licence plates are short and often have a blue tinge or a hint of green on the left when blurred.
All car coverage in Guatemala features a grey Street View car with a visible roof rack and side mirrors, a car only shared with Laos in tropical regions.
Guatemala has a tropical climate and is largely covered by rainforests.
Guatemalan architecture features pastel-painted stone houses with rusted metal roofs or buildings made of exposed white brick.
Guatemalan roads typically have solid white outer lines and a single yellow middle line, which are noticeably thinner than those in Mexico.
Guatemala, like Mexico and Panama, uses the word “ALTO” on its stop signs.
Utility poles in Guatemala are very commonly painted pink, green, or a combination of both.
Guatemala has a relatively low amount of coverage, with even less in the north.
The geography of Guatemala is characterized by a mountainous central region, with flat plains in the north and south.
Southern Guatemala is characterized by completely flat agricultural land and is more developed than the northern plains.
Central Guatemala is predominantly mountainous.
Northern Guatemala is mostly flat but often features a slightly rolling landscape or some hills, unlike the complete flatness of the south.
Oil palm plantations are concentrated in the southwest and just north of the central mountains.
Completely green utility poles are mainly found in the southeast, with some occurrences in the east and far northeast. They often have small pole plates that can help identify the road.
Most green utility poles feature a white pole plate where the top two characters identify the specific road.
In most of Guatemala, the line on the top right bar of the Google car's roof rack is facing forward.
In southeastern Guatemala, the line on the roof rack bar is facing backwards.
A blue rope can often be seen on the bottom right bar of the roof rack in regions where the bar faces backward.
In the south and northeast, the backwards-facing bar is also present, but the bottom right bar is missing its thin black cap.
Phone numbers starting with a 2 are unique to Guatemala City.
Phone numbers starting with 6 are unique to the Guatemala Department. Numbers starting with 7 are found outside this department, while 3, 4, or 5 can be found anywhere.
Lago de Atitlán is the largest lake in Guatemala's mountainous region, surrounded by mountains and volcanoes.
A small dirt road runs through a dense jungle north of Tikal in the far north.
Small white bollards with two black stripes are found on Road 1 northeast of Quetzaltenango.
The PET-11 south of Las Pozas is recognizable by its rolling landscape and a straight north-south road angle.
The CA9 between Escuintla and the coast is a divided highway with concrete pavement.
West of Tikal, a trekker covers several prominent Mayan temples, which are the largest and most intact ruins on Guatemalan Street View.
White rectangular stickers with the word ‘electricista’ are a unique clue for Guatemala City.
